title: Equality & Minority Rights
hook: Majority rule can become majority tyranny. Equality before the law and minority rights are how democracies stop the many from trampling the few.
key_points: Equality before the law means the law applies to everyone alike, without arbitrary distinction.
Minority rights protect groups who can be consistently outvoted by a majority.
They guard against 'tyranny of the majority' — using democratic power to oppress a minority.
Anti-discrimination rules and protected freedoms put some matters beyond a simple majority vote.
content_html: Democracy is rule by the majority — but unrestrained majority rule contains a danger that thoughtful observers have warned about for centuries: a permanent majority can use its numbers to oppress a minority entirely through legitimate votes. This is the "tyranny of the majority." Equality before the law and minority rights are the safeguards democracies build against it, ensuring that winning an election does not mean winning the power to do anything at all to those who lost.
extra_html: Equality before the law is the baseline: the law applies to everyone alike, with no one placed above it and no group singled out for worse treatment without genuine justification. Minority rights go further, specifically protecting groups — defined by religion, ethnicity, language, or other traits — who can be consistently outvoted. Encyclopaedia Britannica notes that modern systems pursue this through equal-protection guarantees and anti-discrimination law, and by entrenching certain freedoms as rights. The deeper mechanism is to place some matters beyond the reach of a simple majority: a vote can decide a tax rate, but it should not be able to strip a minority of its basic liberties. In this sense, minority rights are not opposed to democracy but part of what makes majority rule tolerable and stable over time.

related.title: Civil Liberties vs Civil Rights
related.hook: Two terms people mix up: liberties are freedoms from government interference; rights are protections to be treated equally.

related.title: What Democracy Means
related.hook: Rule by the people: a system where political power ultimately traces back to citizens, usually through regular, free elections.

related.title: Due Process
related.hook: Due process is the promise that the state can't take your liberty or property on a whim — it must follow fair, known rules before it acts against you.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'equality before the law' mean?
flashcards.back_html: That the law applies to everyone alike, without arbitrary distinction — no one is above it and no group is singled out without justification.

flashcards.prompt: What problem do minority rights guard against?

choices.text: The 'tyranny of the majority' — using democratic power to oppress a minority
The risk that too few people vote in elections
Governments spending too little on defense

flashcards.explanation_html: Because a permanent majority could always outvote a minority, rights protect groups from being oppressed through ordinary democratic power.

flashcards.prompt: How do protected rights limit majority rule?

choices.text: They place some freedoms beyond the reach of a simple majority vote
They let minorities overrule every majority decision

flashcards.explanation_html: Putting certain freedoms and protections off-limits to ordinary majorities stops democratic power from being used to strip a minority's basic rights.
